verbalization: Oxybenzone, through its interaction with the splicing factor, proline- and glutamine-rich, appears to be indirectly linked to the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. This relationship is mediated by a biochemical pathway involving a metabolite, (2S)-5-methoxy-2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-2,3-dihydro-1-benzofuran, which acts as a target of oxybenzone. The splicing factor, proline- and glutamine-rich, is a key player in the regulation of gene expression, and its interaction with the metabolite suggests a potential role in modulating the activity of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The indirect nature of this connection highlights the complexity of the biological processes involved, where multiple molecular interactions contribute to the overall effect. The evidence supports a mechanism where oxybenzone influences the expression or function of the splicing factor, which in turn affects the transporter, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
